items.title: The normalization in a reduced scheme is a finite morphism over a field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact morphism f: Y to X of locally algebraic schemes over a field k with Y reduced, the lemma shows that the normalization X' of X in Y is finite over X (statement lines 4969-4975). The proof first verifies that the definition of the normalization in Y applies in this setting: Y is quasi-separated because locally algebraic schemes over a field are locally Noetherian, hence so is the morphism, so the definition is available (proof lines 4978-4984). Finiteness then follows from the general finiteness statement for normalizations in Nagata schemes, using that locally algebraic schemes are locally Noetherian and Nagata (proof lines 4984-4989). The claim is H2: two checks of hypotheses plus one cited finiteness theorem, with the local algebraicity being used twice for different purposes.
